senses.gloss:
DIP (v. t.):
I To plunge or immerse: मज्जयति
(c. of मस्ज्,)
the youths were d. d in the fair dame
with all their soul:
सर्वात्मनैव सुतनौ युवभिर्मज्जे,
N.
II To wet: q. v.: क्लेदयति (c. of क्लिद्).
III To dip out: i. e. to take out: q. v.

DIP (v. i.):
I To immerse (lit. and fig.):
मज्जति (भस्ज्, c. l.).
II To d. into (books etc.):
चुम्बति (चुम्ब्, c. l.).

DIP (subs.):
I Immersion: मज्जनम्।
II In-
-clination, slope,: q. v.

DIPLOMACY:
I In gen. sense: सामन् (n.),
these are the five forms of d. noted by those
skilled in its practice:
इति सामप्रयोगज्ञैः साम पञ्च-
विधं स्भृतम्, Ka.;
the milk ocean was churned
by d.:
क्षीराब्धिर्मथितः साभ्ना, Ka.
II Envoys:
दूतवर्गः।

DIPLOMATIST: सामप्रयोगज्ञः, Ka, and sim.
comp. s.
